# mcp


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard way for an AI agent, such
as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, to discover and call tools that run
outside it. This module offers fossick’s functions as MCP tools. The
agent sees each tool’s name, arguments and docstring, so the docstrings
here are written for the agent and say when to use each option. They are
the tools’ interface and are left longer than the docstrings elsewhere
in fossick.

The tools take the same arguments as the Python functions they wrap,
plus a limit on how much text they return, such as `max_chars`. Long
results are cut at that limit and end with a note saying how many
characters were cut, so an agent knows to ask for more. Results are
converted to plain JSON types before they are returned. The server talks
over standard input and output by default.

### research

``` python
def research(
    query:str, n:int=5, google:bool=False, region:str='auto', timelimit:str | None=None, sel:str | None=None,
    chars:int=4000
)->dict:
```

*Question -\> cited answer: search, read the top n* readable\* results
in parallel (auto-escalating past bot walls, skipping bot-wall/empty
pages and backfilling), return {query, sources, digest, dropped,
region}. digest is cited markdown, one \## section per source, trimmed
to the passages that answer the query and headed with the date the
source says it was published. region is a ddgs ‘country-lang’ code, or
‘auto’ to read the country off the query — set it whenever the answer
depends on jurisdiction or market. timelimit d|w|m|y keeps only recent
sources.\*

### web_search

``` python
def web_search(
    query:str, n:int=10, category:str='text', region:str='auto', timelimit:str | None=None, google:bool=False
)->list:
```

*Search the web via ddgs metasearch (no API key). category:
text|images|news|videos|books. region is a ddgs ‘country-lang’ code, or
‘auto’ to read the country off the query — pass it whenever the answer
depends on where you are (law, price, availability). timelimit d|w|m|y
keeps only recent results. google=True gives real Google ranking via a
stealth browser (slow — only when you need Google).*

## Hidden APIs

[`find_hidden_apis`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#find_hidden_apis)
and
[`capture_network`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#capture_network)
record the background requests a page makes and number them. The server
keeps the list from the most recent of those calls, and
[`replay_capture`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#replay_capture)
sends request number `capture_id` from it again as a plain HTTP call
with the browser’s cookies.
[`paginate_api`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#paginate_api)
reads every page of a JSON API, and returns at most `max_items` items.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L223"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->list:
```

## Browser and shop

[`browse`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#browse) opens
a page in the debug Chrome and returns its snapshot. The server
remembers that page, and the `page_*` tools act on it until the next
[`browse`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#browse). The
`shop_*` tools work the same way on one shopping session, opened by
[`shop_open`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_open);
they wrap `fossick.shop`.

## Connecting a client

``` sh
uvx fossick-mcp          # standard input and output
fossick-mcp --http       # Streamable HTTP
```

Configure your agent to run the first command as an MCP server. If
fossick is already a dependency of your project, `uv run fossick-mcp`
uses the project’s environment instead of installing a separate copy.
